Character encoding-ASCII
ASCII - American Standard Code for Information Interchange
A standard that assigns numbers from 0 - 127 to English letters, numbers, punctuation marks and control codes. 
7-bit code (128 characters)
95 printable (letters, digits, punctuation, space, etc.) 
33 control (codes originally used to control terminals, printers, communication, or text formatting – Esc=Escape)

Character	Decimal	Binary
A	65	01000001
B	66	01000010
C	67	01000011
a	97	01100001
b	98	01100010

units.label: slide 8
units.text:
Character encoding-Unicode
Computers store bytes, not “U+010C”.
A Unicode code point is a unique numerical ID number assigned to represent a character, symbol, or control action in the Unicode Standard
So how do we turn Unicode code points into bytes?

units.label: slide 9
units.text:
UTF-8
UTF-8 (Unicode Transformation Format – 8-bit)
A variable-length character encoding for Unicode.
Variable-length means different characters can use different amounts of storage: some use 1 byte, others 2, 3, or 4 bytes. 
Converts each Unicode character into a specific sequence of 1 to 4 bytes 
ASCII characters keep the same one-byte values
